title: Dry dual-stage lithography and ASML’s immersion prototype
outcome: The dry AT:1150 supplied the lens and AT platform that ASML adapted for the AT:1150i immersion prototype. The dry platform carried forward the dual-stage arrangement already shipped in the AT:750.
findings: ASML announced dual-stage products in December 2000 and reported shipping a production AT:750 to TSMC by 16 September 2001. The 2002 Form 20-F names both the KrF AT:750 and ArF AT:1150 in the AT family.

The 2003 Analyst Day proof-of-concept slides identify the converted 1150 lens and liquid-handling changes to the AT platform. Wafer measurement remained in air on the other stage. In the supplier’s test of a 130 nm isolated contact hole, the prototype depth of focus was 1.2 µm, more than twice the dry AT:1150 comparison.

Albany NanoTech reported its installation and initial qualification by 26 August 2004. EDN’s contemporary reporting identifies the retrofit, with a separate source of testimony in its interview with IBM’s lithography director about the intended defect research. An IBM-led study with ASML coauthors subsequently reported experimental confirmation of a depth-of-focus gain and identified the prototype model.
ASML’s annual filing reports three pre-production deliveries in the second half of 2004. The existing N45LP and 40 nm records concern different foundry milestones.
frontier: Locate a dated AT:1150 launch, shipment or installation record, or an original ASML or ZEISS design history identifying optical or mechanical parts inherited from the dry AT:1100 or PAS 5500/1150.
Trace the 2002 Form 20-F’s statement that TWINSCAN used production-proven PAS 5500 elements to an engineering paper, subsystem specification or tool comparison that identifies those elements.
Look for the original TSMC 2004 Cymer symposium material or exposure logs identifying the ASML model used for the 90 nm SRAM trial.

screen: Searched the current discovery, source and lead records for AT:1150, AT:750, TWINSCAN, PAS 5500, dual-stage, ArF and projection lithography. The existing ASML immersion node gained the link and dated deployment, shipment and paper events. Its TSMC recipient was already linked at programme scope. The EUV Alpha Demo is a separate apparatus.
limits: Shipment, installation, qualification, experiment and customer volume production are distinct. The dry genealogy concerns the platform and the prototype lens. Exact dry AT:1150 launch, AT:1100 component descent, industry priority and the TSMC 2004 test model remain open.
